title: Verifier‑Assisted versus LLM‑Only Pre‑deployment Network‑Change Validation: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We measured whether adding a deterministic pre‑deployment verifier (with at most one automated repair) increases the fraction of intent‑driven configuration proposals that pass semantic validation compared with accepting a single LLM candidate. In a preregistered paired design (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) we executed 300 paired intents (100 per difficulty stratum) using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic NetOps validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Each pair evaluated the same single shared_initial candidate under two conditions: baseline (accept single shot) and guarded (deterministic validation and ≤1 automated repair). Results: baseline 299/300 unflagged passes (0.9966667), guarded 300/300 (1.0); paired contingency n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; absolute paired difference = 0.0033333; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00,0.01] (bootstrap_seed = 1729, B = 10000). Under the supplied synthetic suite and model, single‑shot generation was near ceiling, limiting observable marginal rescue by the guarded pipeline. All preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts are archived with the study id to support reproducible follow‑ups that vary estimand conditioning, model strength, or repair budget.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to network operations (NetOps) tasks such as intent→configuration translation, template synthesis, and automated repair. Operators require semantic guarantees—sequencing, reachability, and policy preservation—that cannot be assessed by syntax alone. Hybrid architectures pairing generative models with deterministic validators and bounded automated repair (generate→validate→repair) aim to reduce operational risk, but the practical benefit of such scaffolds depends on the experimental estimand (what is held fixed), the generator's single‑shot quality, the validator's expressiveness, and the allowed repair budget.

We preregistered a paired experiment (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) that isolates the deterministic rescue utility of a validator and limited automated repair applied to the very same model candidate. For each intent we produced one shared_initial candidate using gpt-5-mini and compared two treatments applied to that identical candidate: baseline (accept the single candidate without correction) and guarded (run a deterministic validator and permit at most one automated repair). The central research question: does adding a deterministic verifier plus at most one automated repair increase the probability that a single LLM candidate passes semantic pre‑deployment validation compared with accepting the same single candidate without repair? Our contributions are (1) a preregistered paired evaluation (N=300 pairs) conditioned on shared_initial candidates that isolates deterministic rescue utility; (2) a fully archived execution and analysis bundle including deterministic validator traces and the single repair; and (3) an evidence‑grounded interpretation of estimator conditioning, ceiling effects, and operational implications for NetOps pipelines.
sections.related_work:
Recent surveys and systems work document extensive activity at the intersection of LLMs and NetOps, covering intent‑based translation, configuration synthesis, automated repair, and tool‑augmented agentic frameworks [https://openalex.org/W4406484968; https://openalex.org/W4411015066; https://openalex.org/W4415275309]. Planner‑centric and tool‑augmented frameworks that call external validators to improve correctness have been proposed and instantiated in prior work [doi:10.1609/aaai.v40i40.40676]. Empirical reports indicate that validator‑assisted generation often reduces errors, but absolute success rates and dominant failure modes vary with task generator, validator coverage, and model strength [https://openalex.org/W4416927413; https://openalex.org/W4404240614].

Two methodological gaps motivated our study. First, many prior comparisons conflate the verifier's deterministic rescue capability with benefits from drawing additional independent model candidates: permitting resampling mixes generator variance with verifier utility. Second, reproducible public benchmarks that emphasize semantic correctness (reachability, sequencing, policy preservation) rather than syntactic validity remain limited. Our paired, shared_initial design directly addresses the first gap by conditioning on a single LLM draw per intent so that observed gains derive solely from deterministic validation and the bounded repair budget.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered study cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001 and froze the primary estimand: the absolute paired difference in the unflagged verifier‑pass proportion (guarded minus baseline) computed on paired cases evaluating the same shared_initial candidate. The preregistration specified design, inclusion/exclusion rules, analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1), multiplicity plan, contamination controls, and reproducible executor inputs. The preregistration also described an optional pilot (n = 60) to estimate discordance and recalibrate power; that pilot was not executed prior to the main run and no post‑preregistration power recalculation was performed (this deviation is explicitly recorded in the Disclosure and Methods).

Task generation and stratification. Tasks were generated deterministically by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 into a synthetic_topology_suite_v1 and stratified into low/medium/high difficulty (100 tasks per stratum). Difficulty metadata (used only for stratified reporting) included changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, and required_command_count; representative intent templates included "shutdown_configure_restore" (medium) and "paired_link_atomic_mtu_change" (hard). A concrete example (representative task task-000001) used in the run: "Migrate edge1 to VLAN 30 and MTU 1600. For safety, shut edge1 down before changing either VLAN or MTU, then restore it to admin up. Do not modify any other interface." Six representative tasks and their reference answers are archived with the run bundle.

Model, orchestration, and candidate sharing. The declared model was gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json). To isolate deterministic rescue of identical model outputs, the pipeline produced a single shared_initial generation per pair. That single shared_initial candidate was evaluated under two conditions: (a) baseline — accept the candidate as‑is; (b) guarded — run the deterministic validator and, if flagged, allow the preregistered single automated repair attempt before a final revalidation. The pipeline intentionally disallowed independent resampling or verifier‑guided iterative generation because those alternative strategies change the estimand.

Validator, scoring, and repair policy. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5, version 5.0) implements the preregistered full_intent_constraint_validation rule: deterministic checks for sequencing constraints (must_be_down_for_fields), preservation of unspecified state, required_command_count, reachability invariants encoded in the synthetic topology, and forbidden‑template protections (protected_interfaces). Scoring is binary per the preregistered rule: unflagged == pass; flagged after allowed repair == failure. The guarded repair policy allowed a single automated repair invocation (repair budget ≤1) that attempted a localized corrective edit to the shared_initial candidate; repair provider traces and validator rechecks were recorded. The manuscript reports a concise semantic summary of the single repair rather than reproducing raw provider transcripts in the body.

Execution accounting, stopping, and missingness handling. The preregistration planned a confirmatory main run of 300 paired intents after an optional pilot. The stopping rule required 300 analyzable pairs per the preregistration; pairs would be excluded only if both pipeline calls failed due to provider/infrastructure outages. Missingness and exclusion handling were implemented exactly as preregistered and are recorded in the execution manifest. All provider call events, cache statistics, and stage counts were logged to enable deterministic reconciliation.
sections.results:
Execution summary and accounting. The hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter executed the confirmatory run: planned_episode_count = 600, completed_episode_count = 600, complete_pair_count = 300, failed_episode_count = 0. Model calls used = 301 (300 shared_initial generations + 1 repair call). Stage counts recorded in the deterministic reconciliation artifact were: shared_initial_generation = 300 and repair = 1. Provider audit counts: hosted_model_call_event_count = 301, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 301, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0, cache_miss_count = 301. Execution timestamps (UTC): started 2026-08-30T09:47:41.113164, completed 2026-08-30T10:17:21.408465. No pairs were excluded and no provider outages occurred.

Marginal and paired outcomes. Condition summary (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline successes = 299/300 (0.9966666667), guarded successes = 300/300 (1.0). The paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is: n11 = 299, n10 = 1 (guarded‑only), n01 = 0 (baseline‑only), n00 = 0. Per‑stratum outcomes: low difficulty 100/100 baseline & guarded; medium 100/100 baseline & guarded; high baseline 99/100 vs guarded 100/100.

Confirmatory inference. The preregistered paired analysis (paired_binary_analysis_v1) produced absolute paired difference = 0.0033333333333332993 (guarded − baseline). The exact two‑sided McNemar equivalent p = 1.0. A paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (bootstrap_seed = 1729, B = 10000) = [0.00, 0.01]. The minimal number of discordant pairs (m = n10 + n01 = 1) controls sensitivity: despite N=300, only one discordant case exists, so inference is limited by the low discordance observed under the shared_initial estimand.

Rescue diagnostic and repair trace summary. The single discordant episode (n10 = 1) triggered the permitted automated repair. Validator traces attribute the initial flag to an omitted sequencing command (must_be_down_for_fields): the shared_initial candidate did not include the required pre‑change 'admin down' for the affected interface prior to VLAN/MTU modification. The automated repair inserted the missing sequencing command; the validator subsequently validated the corrected configuration (valid == true). The low‑level repair provider trace and full validator trace are archived in the run bundle and indexed in the execution manifest; the manuscript reports the concise semantic summary above to preserve operational focus.

Missingness, contamination, and reconciliation. Analysis/missingness_summary.csv records complete_pairs = 300 and zero failed or unscorable episodes. Contamination checks and the contamination_summary.csv are empty. Deterministic reconciliation confirms episode accounting consistency and provider call audit: all deterministic consistency checks passed. These artifacts permit independent re‑execution of the confirmatory calculations by another deterministic analysis executor.
sections.discussion:
Estimator conditioning and operational interpretation. The shared_initial estimand conditions on a single LLM draw per intent and therefore measures only deterministic validator/repair rescue applied to that shared candidate. This estimand corresponds to operational workflows in which a single model call is normative and deterministic auditing plus bounded automated repair is the only corrective mechanism. It intentionally excludes verifier benefits that would arise from allowing independent alternative LLM candidates per condition (resampling, iterative generation, or verifier‑guided steering); those alternative workflows are distinct estimands that can and should be evaluated separately. We explicitly remind readers that the preregistered pilot to estimate discordance was not run and therefore no post‑preregistration power recalculation was performed.

Ceiling effects, power, and practical significance. The baseline near‑ceiling (299/300) reduced observed discordance and thus inferential sensitivity for small absolute improvements. The preregistered power target assumed an appreciable baseline discordance; in practice, when single‑shot generator quality is high on a chosen synthetic suite, the expected rescue mass for a bounded repair budget may be small. Operationally, when single‑shot generation is near perfect for the sampled workload, the marginal operational value of a guarded scaffold (with the same single candidate) is small; organizations should evaluate whether permitting resampling or expanding repair budgets better meets safety objectives.

Validator coverage and failure‑mode dependence. The deterministic validator encoded sequencing, preservation, required_command_count, reachability invariants, and forbidden‑template checks. The dominant observed failure mode in this synthetic suite was sequencing omission; reachability or forbidden‑template violations did not appear at scale. This distribution is a property of the deterministic task generator and the chosen difficulty stratification and may differ in production workloads where topological complexity, device heterogeneity, or unmodeled invariants increase verifier marginal utility.

Operational recommendations. Match the evaluated estimand to the intended production workflow. If operations accept a single model call and desire deterministic safeguard + bounded automatic repair, the shared_initial analysis here is directly relevant. If the operational policy allows multiple candidate draws, resampling or verifier‑guided candidate selection should be evaluated as a separate estimand because it can materially increase rescue opportunities. For higher assurance, expand the repair budget, permit verifier‑guided iterative generation, or use stronger domain‑tuned generation models.

Reproducibility, artifacts, and deterministic audit. All preregistration documents, task manifests, model configuration, raw responses, provider traces, validator traces, analysis CSVs (analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/missingness_summary.csv), deterministic reconciliation, and analysis logs are archived with the study id. Analysis parameters (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729) and the exact executor outputs are recorded. Deterministic reconciliation confirms episode accounting and provider call audit counts. These artifacts permit independent verification of reported numeric summaries and re‑execution of the confirmatory calculations by another deterministic analysis executor.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered, artifact‑archived paired comparison between a verifier‑assisted pipeline (deterministic validator + ≤1 automated repair) and accepting a single‑shot LLM candidate under the shared_initial estimand on 300 synthetic NetOps intents using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Baseline single‑shot generation produced 299/300 unflagged verifier passes and the guarded pipeline 300/300, yielding an absolute paired improvement of 0.00333 (exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI [0.00,0.01]). The near‑ceiling baseline limits inferential sensitivity for small absolute improvements under the shared_initial estimand. We release the preregistration id, execution and analysis artifacts, representative task manifests, and validator traces in the archived run bundle to enable reproducible follow‑ups that vary estimand choice, model strength, or repair strategies.

limitations: Synthetic benchmark: tasks and topologies were generated by the preregistered deterministic task generator; real‑world heterogeneity may expose different failure modes and increase verifier marginal utility.
Single model and validator: only gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 were evaluated; results may not generalize to other LLMs or richer/diverse validators.

Ceiling effect: baseline single‑shot performance was near 100% on this suite (299/300), producing limited discordance and reduced power to detect small absolute improvements relative to larger pre‑specified targets.
Pilot not executed: the preregistered pilot intended for discordance estimation and power calibration was not run; no post‑preregistration power recalculation was performed.

Estimand conditioning: the shared_initial protocol conditions the estimand on a single LLM candidate and therefore does not measure verifier benefit that would arise from allowing independent alternative LLM candidates per condition.
Repair budget: the guarded condition permitted at most one automated repair per pair; larger or iterative repair strategies may yield different outcomes.
